##### R2-G23-01: Playable rule kernel
**Spec directory:** `specs/521-erosion-painter-playable-rule-kernel/` • **Functional requirement:** Implement deterministic state transition and exact win/failure evaluation. **Unique game objective:** sculpt hills and rainfall patterns until erosion carves a prescribed canyon network. **Domain algorithm:** water flux obeys local downhill differences; erode min(k*flow, sediment capacity); deposition restores sediment; clamps conserve material ledger. **Reference solver:** iterative heightfield transport with deterministic hydraulic approximations and seed replay. **Required Stage Two dependencies:** R2-F01, R2-F02, R2-F03, R2-F04, R2-F05, R2-F06, R2-F07, R2-F17, R2-F18, R2-F22, R2-F23, R2-F24, R2-F25, R2-F26, R2-F27, R2-F28, R2-F29, R2-F30, R2-F31, R2-F32, R2-F33, R2-F34.

Device-specific proof is **only planned here** until after all 25 new game targets pass simulator lock.

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.
#### 6.23.12. Seed-by-seed production-level acceptance and replay contracts
Each numbered stage has *seven mandatory acceptance facets* produced by deterministic test generation. Output below enumerates the complete release catalog: QA should create all indicated artifacts and compare them to `ContentManifest.json`. The same replay witness is consumed by CPU-only unit tests and by simulator gameplay on a selected stratified subset. A stage that lacks one facet is `BLOCKED_CONTENT`, not `PASSED`.

#### 6.23.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** thermal/load of repeated high-res terrain; simulate low-res and render adaptively. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `terrain brush` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** mass ledger terrain+sediment and outlet graph stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `ErosionPainter` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `ErosionPainter` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `ErosionPainter` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `mesas dissolving into shining rivulets under spectacular algorithmic weather`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.23.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** thermal/load of repeated high-res terrain; simulate low-res and render adaptively. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `sculpt` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

### 24. Crystal Quarry — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G24` • **Source candidate:** `G334` • **Category:** Terrain alchemy • **Comparative rank:** 24/25 • **Research score:** 92.9/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 86 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Choose fracture paths to reveal a target gem network in rock. **Signature spectacle:** black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations. **Objective:** choose break lines to expose a hidden gem network in a procedural rock body. **A failure:** critical gem is destroyed or energy limit reached. **A victory:** all target seam nodes exposed with host rock stability preserved.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific terrain-contained voxel fracture network system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag guided cleavage stroke, tap inspect mineral glow, rotate core. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.24.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** terrain-contained voxel fracture network. **Proposed authoritative law:** rock consists of bounded convex chunks from deterministic Voronoi seeds; split along known planes, not dynamic brittle FEM. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is seeded lattice graph with cut-set path planning and exposed target constraints. **Truth metric:** reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “all target seam nodes exposed with host rock stability preserved” using `reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “critical gem is destroyed or energy limit reached”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.
```swift

    let witnessInputDigest: String
}

    var tick: UInt64
    var actionsSpent: Int
    var controlParameters: [Double]
    var objectiveResidual: Double
    var phase: String
    var revision: UInt64
}
// Required: deterministic reducer, reversible action stack, solver certificate,
// CPU-only replay tests, and renderer consumption of immutable snapshots.
// Game objective: choose break lines to expose a hidden gem network in a procedural rock body.

// Solver: seeded lattice graph with cut-set path planning and exposed target constraints.
```

#### 6.24.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations. **Required geometry:** deterministic Voronoi chunk meshes with internal seam shader. **Signature shader:** glowing mineral seams emerge through geometric stone fractures; Deterministic heightfields, erosion approximation, instanced scenery and raster-free sky. **Palette:** slate obsidian, emerald and molten rose. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.24.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 86 levels. **Prototype:** graded mineral clusters and multi-step exposure puzzles. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

**Build-time catalog validation:** for every row, enforce a nonempty title, manifest schema version, puzzle seed, exact initial state, declared target, at least one valid solver-produced move trace, difficulty metrics, stable score threshold, and a procedurally generated hero frame. Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.24.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/CrystalQuarry/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.24.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `fracture` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “Critical gem is destroyed or energy limit reached”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

#### 6.24.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** fracture robustness and overly similar visuals to Faceted Forge; target differs as exploration not shaping solids. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `fracture` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** reachable exposed seam count and stable chunk adjacency stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `CrystalQuarry` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `CrystalQuarry` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `CrystalQuarry` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `black slate parting to show incandescent crystalline constellations`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.24.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** fracture robustness and overly similar visuals to Faceted Forge; target differs as exploration not shaping solids. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `mine` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

### 25. Starlight Surveyors — fully specified proposed game design
**Game spec ID:** `R2-G25` • **Source candidate:** `G122` • **Category:** Cosmic puzzles • **Comparative rank:** 25/25 • **Research score:** 92.84/100 (concept judgment only) • **Complete paid app:** $3.99 upfront • **Content target:** 82 solver-certified stages • **Primary timestep:** 0.008333 s • **No ads/no IAP/no image assets**.
**Player fantasy:** Rotate a 3D observatory until starlight aligns through viewports. **Signature spectacle:** geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument. **Objective:** rotate a three-axis observatory until projected star rays align through multiple lens apertures. **A failure:** a required ray passes outside a viewport on a checkpoint tick. **A victory:** all designated rays intersect their required lenses in correct sequence.
**Critical differentiation:** compare this specific perspective projection alignment system to all original 25 VisualCore apps, and to the other 24 Round Two games. Its distinct state machine, verbs, input interactions, solution representation and original level grammar must stand on their own; do not publish a different skin over an existing game.
#### 6.25.1. Player journey and minute-by-minute first play

**Main modes:** Play (campaign), Practice (unlimited undo + hints), Daily-Seed Equivalent (offline local date converted into stable seed, no servers or streak coercion), Gallery (player-solved scenes), Accessibility Settings (not hidden behind gear-only glyph), and Device Diagnostics (DEBUG/automation only). Default campaign never requires fast reflexes, loud audio, external sensor permission or online connection.
**Controls:** drag gimbals, pinch zoom lens, tap lock orientation. Implement gesture arbitration with accessible stepper controls for all essential state changes; camera motion must not change puzzle semantics. Highlight currently selected control with a geometric outline and VoiceOver description. Keyboard/controller may be optional but cannot be the only solution route.
#### 6.25.2. Mathematical state, exact rules and victory proof
**Simulation domain:** perspective projection alignment. **Proposed authoritative law:** camera basis R=RzRyRx; project each star into a normalized pinhole viewport with stable near-plane constraints. **Fixed-step interval:** 0.008333 s, with tick-indexed inputs. The reference solver is finite camera-angle/target quantization search and analytic projective ray intersection. **Truth metric:** reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors.
**State machine:** `uninitialized → loading → tutorial → playing ↔ paused → {won, failed} → result → next-level`; explicit paths for `reload`, `resume`, `undo`, `redo`, `content-corrupt`, `renderer-unavailable`, `host-backgrounded`, `device-locked`, `migration-needed`. A rendering failure may interrupt display but must never quietly mutate logical win state.
**Numerical design:** use explicit finite-number validation, fixed bounded arrays, normalized viewport coordinates independent of resolution, stable sample-order and a maximum CPU work budget per tick. Avoid nondeterministic dictionary iteration in seeded rule evaluation. Where trigonometric floating point is unavoidable, test semantic tolerance bands and hashes of canonical quantized state rather than assert identical floating-point bit patterns across architectures.
**Action validation:** every mutation is an append-only action record `(schemaVersion, levelSeed, tick, controlID, parameter, previousDigest, nextDigest)`. Reject out-of-range positions, invalid scene IDs, excess move budgets, non-finite values, stale replay hashes and actions at a terminal state. Actions from a paused game must queue or be rejected according to the documented state machine, never partially apply.
**Win evaluator (game-specific):** require “all designated rays intersect their required lenses in correct sequence” using `reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors`; success is decided in CPU reference logic, independently of shader color or GL frame rate. Failure evaluator: “a required ray passes outside a viewport on a checkpoint tick”. Include strict edge tests at tolerance boundary±epsilon, max action budget and zero-time cases.

#### 6.25.4. Three-dimensional visual identity built with code only
**Hero scene:** geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument. **Required geometry:** procedural star sprites as points, gimbal meshes and ray tubes. **Signature shader:** Parametric star volumes, glowing triangulation rays and projection-matched constellations. **Palette:** deep ink, pearl rays and gold gears. **Prohibited:** prompt-generated textures, purchased meshed props, downloaded photo backgrounds, manual character animation, pre-rendered fake 3D scenes or external art-service dependencies.
**Frame architecture:** compute CPU simulation snapshot → game scene adapter serializes validated parameter arrays → shared VisualCore scene graph chooses mesh/instance buffers → actual GL ES/ANGLE context compiles bounded shader permutation → draw opaque depth geometry → draw geometry-aware emissive/glow layer → optional half-resolution post glow → composite with native SwiftUI game HUD. Shader compilation must be prewarmed or amortized; no unbounded compile on live gesture.
**Camera decisions:** prefer authored-perspective/isometric starting pose readable on iPhone 15; support constrained two-finger orbit rather than free navigation, large hit targets, reset camera, and near/far planes based on actual scene bounds. Maintain consistent world-up and avoid fragile `lookAt` singularities near vertical orbit. Use right-handed world coordinates unless Stage One adopts another convention; insert explicit transform adapter.
**Material plan:** procedural high-frequency detail through analytic normals, edge-distance glows, gradient fields, fresnel-like highlights and light-proxy geometry. Do not promise physically accurate volumetric fog or real caustics; label such effects as convincing mobile approximations. If GPU extensions are absent on D3, switch to layered geometry, not replacement raster assets.
**Quality tiers:** Tier 0 D3-safe minimal layers, Tier 1 balanced layers, Tier 2 optional dense spectacle. Each tier **must** preserve the same objective, scene coordinate system, collision/interaction state and accessible indicators; it changes only tessellation, sample count, blur scale, bloom iterations, antialias mode and visual trails. Log the selected tier and reason for adaptation.
**Screenshots:** provide deterministic scripted captures for hero, tutorial, normal play, near-win, win and failure. These are **real simulator/device render captures** rather than invented promotional images. A human may later curate marketing, but no human-authored art is required to produce the game.
#### 6.25.5. Detailed content-production and difficulty design
**Total proposed production catalog:** 82 levels. **Prototype:** angle-grid and multi-aperture puzzles. **Generation method:** seed-specific geometry and target parameters are constructed before solver certification. If candidate generation yields no valid solution or multiple indistinguishable answers in a unique-answer tier, reject the seed and move deterministically to the next salt. No dynamic server content or advertisements are needed.
**Difficulty bands:** Band 1 teaches a single action and permits reversible mistakes; Band 2 combines two controls; Band 3 introduces explicit constraints; Band 4 asks for strategic order and limited resources; Band 5 is optional mastery with richer visuals, but not unfair micro-target gestures. All bands keep a CPU-computable witness; “hard” must mean harder decisions, not greater visual clutter or inaccessible colors.

Refuse a release build if witness count, duplicates or content hashes deviate unexpectedly. Avoid creating dozens of cosmetically varied levels lacking new decisions.
#### 6.25.6. Persistence, privacy and failure recovery
Canonical local save path: `Application Support/StarlightSurveyors/v1/progress.json`, stored via atomic temporary write + checksum validation, with level ID, seed, content schema, score, best solution moves, preferences and player-generated replay IDs. No account identifier, advertising ID, arbitrary app telemetry, audio recording or remote service. Only the game writes its own `UserDefaults` keys under a namespaced prefix; verify the container and allow OS-managed Metal/StoreKit artifacts to be recognized as system artifacts rather than wrongly treating them as hidden tracking.
Handle missing/old/corrupt saves deterministically: classify corruption, preserve a diagnostic copy without private secrets, load a safe default catalog, show a concise visible recovery message, and never erase solved levels silently. If a generated content version changes, migrate by stable level ID and offer deterministic fallback. Save when leaving gameplay and after completed levels; do not save every render frame.
#### 6.25.7. Accessibility, child-suitable design and responsible visual spectacle
Every action on `observatory` has a named native control with stepwise alternative to gestures; labels describe current values, acceptable ranges and next affordance without relying on hue or sound. Offer a camera reset, reversible moves, large touch targets, VoiceOver reading of objective residual `reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors`, scaled native text, no mandatory timed challenges, no flicker-dependent solutions and respectful Reduce Motion/Reduce Flashing handling. A premium player should never be prompted to buy extra content, watch ads, share contact lists or sign in.
**Failure-specific coaching:** when the solver detects a dead-end state, explain the violated constraint in accessible text, e.g. domain-specific “A required ray passes outside a viewport on a checkpoint tick”, offer undo and optional progressive hint. Avoid generic “Wrong!” messages and do not auto-solve before asking; the goal is a satisfying mental challenge, not a screensaver.

| `Apps/StarlightSurveyors/App/StarlightSurveyorsApp.swift` | @main scene and application lifecycle, no direct shader logic |
| `Apps/StarlightSurveyors/App/StarlightSurveyorsCoordinator.swift` | session navigation and restoration, entitlement-free paid-once app |
| `Apps/StarlightSurveyors/App/RootScene.swift` | SwiftUI view hierarchy with exactly one GL rendering host |
| `Apps/StarlightSurveyors/UI/StarlightSurveyorsHUD.swift` | accessible goal and state readout |
| `Apps/StarlightSurveyors/UI/StarlightSurveyorsGestureOverlay.swift` | arbitrate touch, choose depth-aware world target |

**Visual golden captures per stage:** generate preview images from source using fixed seed, camera matrix, GL context capability tier and shader commit: scene-initial, hover/drag, near-win, win, lose, accessibility grayscale, reduced motion and reduced flash. Label GPU-specific baselines; do not overwrite prior goldens automatically because that can hide regressions. A zero-pixel “pass” without visual inspection is insufficient to establish commercial-quality art.

#### 6.25.13. Hardware-campaign design; no physical testing until implementation lock
**Game-specific measurement risk:** orientation can be disorienting; always show axes and a reset pose. **Representative stress:** maximize visible `observatory` instances, trigger repeated controlled interactions for thirty minutes and run a second battery-friendly reduced effects tier. **Semantic truth:** reprojection residual and aperture intersection errors stays invariant across all quality tiers and device refresh rates.
- **D1 iPhone15,4, recorded iOS 27.0.1 24A446:** install exact signed `StarlightSurveyors` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Reference touch-size and visual readability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D2 iPad17,3, recorded iPadOS 27.2 24B119:** install exact signed `StarlightSurveyors` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. High-density/large-aspect multitouch is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
- **D3 iPad15,7, recorded iPadOS 26.5 23F77:** install exact signed `StarlightSurveyors` Automation build; verify `devicectl` live hardware and build; run first launch, scripted success/failure/replay, direct 30-minute stress mode, screenshot of signature `geometric constellations crystallizing into a radiant planetary instrument`, process exit, memory/thermal/frame samples and 5-second “what is this game?” screenshot review. Lowest performance / backward availability is the primary concern. Record JSON + `.xcresult` if XCTest available and never mark pass from an emulator. D3 is never updated.
**Shipping-build separation:** `ROUND2_AUTOMATION` (or the user-approved equivalent) is added only to a specific Release-like test configuration; check `nm -U` and compile flags to ensure the commercial Release target contains no automation endpoints. Every automation mode writes bounded JSON to Documents then exits; a mode that never exits makes the next sequential device job unreliable.
#### 6.25.14. Test-driven risks, distinctiveness challenge and decision gate
**Primary technical uncertainty:** orientation can be disorienting; always show axes and a reset pose. **Strongest commercial objection:** the beautiful effect could be a tech demo rather than a meaningful game. Address this by having the deterministic solver certify the rules and a playable tutorial demonstrate player choices; build an originality matrix with gameplay verb `align` against each of the other 24 Stage Two titles and original 25 Stage One products.
**Minimum internal release readiness:** (a) all planned levels generated, tested and playable; (b) all ten feature specs converged, with independent commands; (c) app bundle builds unsigned for both simulator runtimes; (d) full 50-scenario/3-environment table passes or each inapplicable test is explicitly justified; (e) full physical D1–D3 evidence exists after implementation lock, not before; (f) graphics judged excellent in recorded hero videos/screenshots; (g) no ad or art-generation dependencies; (h) independent paid-game product identity passes copycat review. Failing any condition leads to targeted repair, combination or honest `NO_GO`, not dummy completion.

## 7. Strict autonomous project schedule and task graph
**The requested chronological split is preserved:** first fully implement and simulator-verify the entire new suite; then run hardware in one D1 → D2 → D3 sequence. Stage Two cannot begin until the original README first-stage lock AND first-stage device campaign evidence are complete. Within Stage Two, simulator/host tests are part of implementation and are allowed continuously; no real-device install, launch or XCTest before Stage Two lock.

### 7.3 Scheduling, human limits and recovery
Claude Code runs in Claude Desktop > Code against the VisualCore local repository. Auto mode, if present and authorized, may reduce routine prompts, but a session may still stop for safety/limits. An optional **native Desktop local scheduled task** may relaunch a continuation prompt; whether this facility is available depends on installed Desktop version/plan. The Mac must remain awake and Desktop open for local tasks. Do not promise that the agent controls its own session lifecycle or can grant macOS permission prompts. If a security/system owner action is unavailable, mark it `BLOCKED_OWNER_ACTION`, preserve context and proceed only with independent unblocked tasks.
**Never write a Python supervisor that shells out to `claude`, `claude -p`, a private model API or an SDK**. A Python scheduler may manage xcodebuild, simctl, devicectl, fixture/test/report programs; the Claude Desktop session is the only AI executor. Avoid bulk pasting a file of slash commands and assuming they execute: Claude must invoke each installed skill and inspect result artifacts in the session.
### 7.4 Session restart and stuck-gate algorithm
```text
on each Desktop Code session start:
  read CLAUDE.md; canonical README chapters; round2.md indexed current section
  inspect git status and actual current source code; do NOT assume memory of prior sessions
  verify round1 exit and Stage Two manifest checksums
  acquire .autonomy/round2-desktop.lock safely (PID and lease, no blind stale-lock deletion)
  choose first dependency-ready NOT_STARTED or failed gate
  set Spec Kit active feature explicitly and verify directory
  execute the next installed skill with the corresponding literal prompt in round2.md
  review spec or code outputs; repair contradictions; run independent commands
  collect exit codes, screenshots/reports, update manifest atomically
  commit reviewed verified work without unauthorized remote actions
  repeat until session limit or gate blocker
  on interruption: release lock when possible, leave next-action pointer and reason

on convergence:
  when tasks appended: execute implementation; fresh tests; converge again
  do not raise CONVERGED if only a plan, empty source files, an agent claim or mocked tests exist

on device campaign:
  reject run if implementation lock source SHA differs from current SHA
  reject run if prior device batch incomplete (D2 cannot start before full D1 batch)
  on targeted hotfix: link previous failed run and new corrected run; retain old evidence
```
## 8. Deterministic build, simulation and device-test command playbook
Commands below are **template commands**. Discover schemes, destinations and exact Xcode syntax on the live Mac before running; replace placeholders based on parsed `xcrun` output rather than hardcoded guessed UDIDs or scheme names. Capture full output to dedicated files; do not hide a failing command behind `|| true`. Set timeout defaults and constrain parallel jobs to avoid Mac contention.
### 8.1 Initial environment and repository checks
```bash
set -euo pipefail
pwd
git status --porcelain=v1
git rev-parse HEAD
git submodule status --recursive
xcodebuild -version
xcrun simctl list devices available --json
xcrun devicectl list devices --json-output Build/round2/devices-current.json
xcodegen --version
python3 --version
specify --help
python3 Tools/python/round2_preflight.py --strict --output docs/test-reports/round1-exit-audit.json
# Above Python tool is a proposed Stage Two deliverable; do not pretend it exists until implemented.
# It MUST refuse to certify Round One without builds, simulator and 75 real-device rows.
```
### 8.2 XcodeGen and simulator commands
```bash
# XcodeGen uses the repository actual configuration; add Stage Two targets, never erase Round One targets.
xcodegen generate
xcodebuild -list -json -project VisualCore.xcodeproj > Build/round2/available_schemes.json
# Scheme path below is a template; discover exact generated project name first.
SCHEME="AuroraLoom"
SIM_26_UDID="<discover from simctl JSON, runtime iOS 26.5>"
SIM_27_UDID="<discover from simctl JSON, runtime iOS 27.2>"
for UDID in "$SIM_26_UDID" "$SIM_27_UDID"; do
  xcodebuild -project VisualCore.xcodeproj -scheme "$SCHEME"     -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,id=$UDID"     -derivedDataPath "Build/round2/DerivedData/$SCHEME"     CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO     -resultBundlePath "Build/round2/Results/$SCHEME-$UDID.xcresult"     -test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 180 test     > "Build/round2/logs/$SCHEME-$UDID.log" 2>&1
  # Inspect xcodebuild exit status and xcresult bundle; do not claim pass from a screenshot.
done
# CPU-only logic packages where applicable:
swift test --package-path Packages/Round2Math
swift test --package-path Packages/Round2Geometry
swift test --package-path Packages/Round2Simulation
```
Use `xcrun xcresulttool --help` to select the supported export/results syntax on this Xcode version. Simulator test results are valid for logic/UI contract and asset production but **never** prove physical-device frame pacing, performance, thermal or audio capture compatibility. Output images should be automatically generated from the renderer and stored as gitignored baseline diagnostics until reviewed. Do not overwrite a known-good reference image just because the image-diff script reports a mismatch.
### 8.3 Pixel and visual validation contract
Build a VisualCore `GraphicsLab` test harness that renders a canonical game hero scene at fixed camera and seed; export raw screenshot + structured semantic scene description (object count, material variant IDs, shader signature, normal/depth checks). Test image histograms, absence of fully black frames, unexpected NaNs/clips and silhouette bounds. Pixel-level comparison must tolerate true differences between GPU implementations and color spaces. A human or explicit owner-design review is still needed to confirm that the result is actually **stunning**; automated pixel checks alone cannot establish aesthetic excellence.


The original ProjectM-iOS owner experience indicates: device locked failures, need to pre-unlock and sometimes set Auto-Lock to Never; owner-controlled first permission prompts, purchase dialogs and system pickers cannot always be automated; device automation should launch, write one finite JSON and exit; initial install launch may only dismiss onboarding. Use a signed release-like automation build with `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS=ROUND2_AUTOMATION`, and verify shipping Release lacks those symbols. Do not copy a ProjectM `PROJECTM_AUTORUN` environment variable into unrelated games; use a new namespaced `ROUND2_AUTORUN`.

**Batch order:** D2 is locked until every D1 game has a terminal machine-readable result (PASS, FAILED or BLOCKED with evidence and explicit campaign policy). D3 is locked until D2 is complete. D3 OS is never touched. ### 8.7 Measurement procedures adopted from ProjectM-iOS
Use at least 200 samples for percentage success criteria; earlier ProjectM work found significant variance with sample sizes around 50. Record ID for **every** sample and break shader load, draw submission, first meaningful frame and input-response apart. Scroll performance uses `CADisplayLink` and on-time/missed frame slots. Battery/thermal tests should monitor OS thermal state and record ambient test conditions when available; do not report private hardware counters as though public SDK exposes them. Privacy audit lists the app container and allowed UserDefaults keys; ignore unrelated OS-managed StoreKit/Metal caches only with documented rationale. App thinning size reports compare actual export variants per model where a baseline exists.
### 8.8 CI, repository, signing and compliance lessons
Use XcodeGen as a pinned reproducible project generator; generated `.xcodeproj` is not committed unless Stage One rules differ. Pin XcodeGen and CMake/Swift tool versions in `docs/toolchain.md` and check them in `verify_environment.py`. Keep proprietary signing data out of version control using optional `Signing.local.xcconfig`; allow unsigned CI and simulator builds (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`). Device build provisioning may need `-allowProvisioningUpdates`, but cannot create team certificates or sign in for the owner. Build cache keys must incorporate ANGLE fork SHA, ProjectM SHA if used, Xcode build, ABI and variant. CI should do compliance/doc test early on Linux, pure SwiftPM logic tests where portable, macOS shader/ANGLE builds, at least one relevant iOS simulator runtime, generic device builds, and no CI assumed to cover direct physical-device tests.
**StoreKit policy differs from original ProjectM:** this Round Two requires **zero IAP**. Preserve general lessons about test-host isolation and product request loops only as defensive awareness. Do not add an IAP flow, local `.storekit` file, fake entitlement switch or Ask to Buy tests if the apps sell only as one-time App Store products; that would invent complexity and change the policy.
### 8.9 Privacy, trademark, legal and art-provenance checklist
Run a source/binary scanner for prohibited ad dependencies, `ASIdentifierManager`, advertising attribution SDKs, StoreKit IAP product request paths, embedded analytics trackers, remote image pipelines, unsigned code downloads, placeholder branding, copied UI art, copyrighted game audio and trademark-confusing titles. Verify copied code licenses including ANGLE, ProjectM and shader snippets from external sources; public GitHub repository does not waive third-party license obligations. MIT for VisualCore itself is not a blanket license for vendored components. Do not offer legal assurances on the basis of a software-only scan; release counsel/owner review remains a separate item.
### 8.10 Distinctive original identities and anti-variant review
Construct a 25×25 pairwise game identity matrix before app-store launch. Each pair compares player objective, required inputs, puzzle state, win scoring, puzzle progression, and screenshot silhouette. If only palette/effect type differs, recommend combining them into a single stronger release or retiring one. Examples of close pairs to scrutinize: **Aurora Loom vs Backwards Aurora**, **Lissajous Labyrinth vs Wave Knot Keeper**, **Nocturne Garden vs Moonlit Mechanism**, **Faceted Forge vs Crystal Quarry**, **Celestial Eclipse Lab vs Apsides Workshop**, **Acoustic Constellator vs Harmonic Bridges**. The preselected 25 are development hypotheses, not permission to ship 25 near-duplicates. Preserve the portfolio list but allow evidence-driven product rationalization before public releases.

## 11. Full source arguments and research lineage
The next section is the **complete, verbatim** AssertionOutlines supplied by the approved Round Two 500-candidate research. The source includes 25 games × 3 claims × 4 reasons × one evidence each = **75 claims, 300 reasons and 300 evidence statements**, plus counterarguments and pivot criteria. They are evidence-based decision arguments, *not* proof of the new games’ profitability or real-device results. Do not silently remove or rewrite them when editing game designs; any new contradictory evidence should be added in a dated addendum and linked to actual tests.
### 11.1. Verbatim Round Two 25-game AssertionOutlines
<!-- BEGIN ORIGINAL ASSERTION OUTLINES: content preserved exactly -->
# VisualCore — Refined Round 2: 25 Complete AssertionOutlines

**As of:** 2026-11-10 | **Scope:** selection from 500 scored casual 3D games | **Build rule:** 100% procedural VisualCore/GLSL/ANGLE/Metal graphics | **Price:** $1.99–$4.99 paid once, **never ads**.

## Reading guide: argument, reasons, evidence, counterarguments

Each game has **exactly three arguable claims**, each with **four reasons**, and each reason with **one explicitly identified evidence item**: 3 × 4 = **12 reason–evidence pairs per game**. Totals: **75 claims, 300 reasons, 300 evidence items**. Arguments are hypotheses to test, not fabricated proof of revenues, excellent graphics, or completed performance benchmarks.

**Evidence-strength legend:** **Observed external** means a reputable public source confirms something about a comparison category or technology; **Analytical/design** means the current written design exhibits the property but a playable build does not yet; **Acceptance contract** is a falsifiable planned test, not a passed test. Market analogs demonstrate possibilities, never sales of the proposed games.

**Do not confuse an argument with a promise:** a company can reject a compelling argument if prototypes, real-device metrics, or acquisition tests falsify its premises. A game must not be called a success because it receives a high heuristic score.

## 01. Aurora Loom — 94.80/100

**Candidate:** `G162` | **Family:** Light and color | **Premium price:** $2.99 | **Visual assessment:** 97.83/100 | **Comparative paid-game score:** 87.73/100.

**Playing fantasy:** weave and phase-shift 3D luminous ribbons into target harmonies. **The moment of wonder:** layered ribbon meshes with wave displacement and fragment interference patterns.

### Claim 1 — The signature visual system is a plausible code-only VisualCore product

**Claim:** A compelling first impression for **Aurora Loom** can plausibly be rendered entirely by GLSL ES and generated geometry, because its primary spectacle is produced by the same rules that players manipulate. This is a feasibility assertion, not a benchmark result.

1. **Reason:** The visible world is expressible as deterministic procedural meshes and shaders, so the design avoids painted hero backgrounds and manual polygon modeling.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the candidate rendering specification proposes “Layered ribbon meshes with wave displacement and fragment interference patterns”; that is an executable algorithmic direction, not a completed screenshot.

2. **Reason:** The project reuses the existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal path instead of inventing another GPU backend for strong moving geometry with responsive lighting.
   **Evidence:** **Observed external technical:** Google documents ANGLE as an OpenGL ES implementation with an iOS Metal backend ([ANGLE repository](https://github.com/google/angle)); this establishes interface viability, not device frame rate.

3. **Reason:** Every hero object can be made from meshes, particles, shader gradients or procedural fields; Aurora Loom does not require an image model or character animator.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the declared content bill of materials contains zero generated-image assets, zero painted textures and zero manually rigged characters; a later repository scan must verify that promise.

4. **Reason:** The renderer can be inspected with repeatable, fixed-seed camera captures and performance counters before art quality is accepted.
   **Evidence:** **Observed external technical:** Apple describes GPU-time, frame pacing and thermal inspection in its [game-performance guidance](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/meet-with-apple/242/); a proposed gate uses the same categories on D3.


### Claim 2 — The mechanic deserves a serious test as a paid-once, no-ad casual game

**Claim:** There is a commercially defensible hypothesis for selling **Aurora Loom** at $2.99 without ads, because the loop has a clear objective, a polished visual payoff and relevant premium-game precedents. This is not a revenue forecast.

1. **Reason:** The loop is understandable as a concrete player action: “Weave and phase-shift 3D luminous ribbons into target harmonies.”
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** a prospective tutorial can show the action and a visible success state in fewer than three gestures; the loop is written in the candidate inventory, but has not yet been tested with players.

2. **Reason:** Players demonstrably purchase some complete iPhone/iPad games rather than only ad-funded products.
   **Evidence:** **Observed external market:** Apple’s [official 2025 U.S. paid iPhone chart](https://apps.apple.com/us/iphone/room/6756363168) lists titles including Balatro, Geometry Dash and Stardew Valley; none proves demand for Aurora Loom.

3. **Reason:** The genre has a neighboring PC example, suggesting a category audience worth examining without copying its protected presentation.
   **Evidence:** **Observed external market:** the [published comparable: Glass Masquerade official Steam store](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/) provides a real title in a related category; reviews and price are not evidence of sales for Aurora Loom.

4. **Reason:** A one-price offline product removes the need for rewarded videos, accounts, subscription churn and paid virtual goods.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the business model is exactly $2.99 upfront with all stages unlocked, no network services, no analytics advertising identifiers, and no IAP dependencies; validate purchaser acceptance before release.


### Claim 3 — A bounded prototype can decide whether this game merits production

**Claim:** **Aurora Loom** is worth a controlled engineering prototype rather than an immediate 25-app launch commitment, because its risks can be made explicit and measured against falsifiable criteria.

1. **Reason:** The game can distinguish itself from directly similar procedural puzzle games with its actual interaction, rather than relying on a palette swap.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the proposed distinguishing action is “Weave and phase-shift 3D luminous ribbons into target harmonies,” with the spectacle “Layered ribbon meshes with wave displacement and fragment interference patterns”; the final originality and trademark review remains unperformed.

2. **Reason:** Seeded rules can produce a complete offline collection of repeatable seeded goals and standalone sessions without a large handmade level-art pipeline.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the content prototype is ten seeded frequency settings whose targets can be evaluated by a numeric tolerance; its generator and fun factor must still be implemented and verified.

3. **Reason:** A reliable automated test can separately determine logical solvability and scene beauty rather than conflating a screenshot with gameplay.
   **Evidence:** **Acceptance contract (not observed):** pass only after level replay agrees with the solver at fixed seeds, screenshot comparisons reveal no missing geometry, and a human reviewer can identify the goal in a blind five-second view.

4. **Reason:** The expensive uncertainty is observable on real hardware: thermal and overdraw risk on D3; crowding among optical/geometry premium games.
   **Evidence:** **Acceptance contract (not observed):** after full-suite implementation lock, run a 30-minute session on D3 iPad A16/iPadOS 26.5, and record GPU frame timing, missed frames, thermals, visual captures and app crashes; reject or downscale if failed.


**Strongest objection:** This may be a beautiful technical demonstration with too little repeatable fun, or a near-duplicate of another VisualCore game. The high score cannot answer that objection.

**Response:** Keep development gated: build the rule “Weave and phase-shift 3D luminous ribbons into target harmonies” before polishing a trailer; measure solving, retries and user comprehension; compare the candidate against other shortlisted mechanisms.

**Kill / pivot criteria:** Stop or combine this idea if a seeded level has no meaningful choice, if real D3 renders fail sustained budgets after quality scaling, if distinctive visual assets require manual art, or if independent players cannot explain the rules. Do not publish near-identical apps to inflate the portfolio.

**Argument verdict:** **PROTOTYPE, NOT GUARANTEED LAUNCH.** The central claim is that a beautiful and interactive code-generated game is *testable*; its commercial desirability is still unproven.

3. **Reason:** Every hero object can be made from meshes, particles, shader gradients or procedural fields; Chrono Constellator does not require an image model or character animator.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the declared content bill of materials contains zero generated-image assets, zero painted textures and zero manually rigged characters; a later repository scan must verify that promise.

4. **Reason:** The renderer can be inspected with repeatable, fixed-seed camera captures and performance counters before art quality is accepted.
   **Evidence:** **Observed external technical:** Apple describes GPU-time, frame pacing and thermal inspection in its [game-performance guidance](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/meet-with-apple/242/); a proposed gate uses the same categories on D3.


### Claim 2 — The mechanic deserves a serious test as a paid-once, no-ad casual game

**Claim:** There is a commercially defensible hypothesis for selling **Chrono Constellator** at $3.99 without ads, because the loop has a clear objective, a polished visual payoff and relevant premium-game precedents. This is not a revenue forecast.

1. **Reason:** The loop is understandable as a concrete player action: “Record and replay a constellation's motion until all stars align.”
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** a prospective tutorial can show the action and a visible success state in fewer than three gestures; the loop is written in the candidate inventory, but has not yet been tested with players.

2. **Reason:** Players demonstrably purchase some complete iPhone/iPad games rather than only ad-funded products.
   **Evidence:** **Observed external market:** Apple’s [official 2025 U.S. paid iPhone chart](https://apps.apple.com/us/iphone/room/6756363168) lists titles including Balatro, Geometry Dash and Stardew Valley; none proves demand for Chrono Constellator.

3. **Reason:** The genre has a neighboring PC example, suggesting a category audience worth examining without copying its protected presentation.
   **Evidence:** **Observed external market:** the [published comparable: Baba Is You official Steam store](https://store.steampowered.com/app/736260/Baba_Is_You/) provides a real title in a related category; reviews and price are not evidence of sales for Chrono Constellator.

4. **Reason:** A one-price offline product removes the need for rewarded videos, accounts, subscription churn and paid virtual goods.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the business model is exactly $3.99 upfront with all stages unlocked, no network services, no analytics advertising identifiers, and no IAP dependencies; validate purchaser acceptance before release.


### Claim 3 — A bounded prototype can decide whether this game merits production

**Claim:** **Chrono Constellator** is worth a controlled engineering prototype rather than an immediate 25-app launch commitment, because its risks can be made explicit and measured against falsifiable criteria.

1. **Reason:** The game can distinguish itself from other time-edit puzzles with its actual interaction, rather than relying on a palette swap.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the proposed distinguishing action is “Record and replay a constellation's motion until all stars align,” with the spectacle “3D star traces accumulate into glowing history ribbons”; the final originality and trademark review remains unperformed.

2. **Reason:** Seeded rules can produce a complete offline collection of short repeatable time loops with an exact final condition without a large handmade level-art pipeline.
   **Evidence:** **Analytical/design:** the content prototype is ten replayable seeded levels with a deterministic solution checker and failure reason; its generator and fun factor must still be implemented and verified.

3. **Reason:** A reliable automated test can separately determine logical solvability and scene beauty rather than conflating a screenshot with gameplay.
   **Evidence:** **Acceptance contract (not observed):** pass only after level replay agrees with the solver at fixed seeds, screenshot comparisons reveal no missing geometry, and a human reviewer can identify the goal in a blind five-second view.

4. **Reason:** The expensive uncertainty is observable on real hardware: thermal and overdraw risk on D3; replay rules may become hard to communicate.
   **Evidence:** **Acceptance contract (not observed):** after full-suite implementation lock, run a 30-minute session on D3 iPad A16/iPadOS 26.5, and record GPU frame timing, missed frames, thermals, visual captures and app crashes; reject or downscale if failed.


**Strongest objection:** This may be a beautiful technical demonstration with too little repeatable fun, or a near-duplicate of another VisualCore game. The high score cannot answer that objection.

**Response:** Keep development gated: build the rule “Record and replay a constellation's motion until all stars align” before polishing a trailer; measure solving, retries and user comprehension; compare the candidate against other shortlisted mechanisms.

**Kill / pivot criteria:** Stop or combine this idea if a seeded level has no meaningful choice, if real D3 renders fail sustained budgets after quality scaling, if distinctive visual assets require manual art, or if independent players cannot explain the rules. Do not publish near-identical apps to inflate the portfolio.

**Argument verdict:** **PROTOTYPE, NOT GUARANTEED LAUNCH.** The central claim is that a beautiful and interactive code-generated game is *testable*; its commercial desirability is still unproven.

   **Evidence:** **Acceptance contract (not observed):** pass only after level replay agrees with the solver at fixed seeds, screenshot comparisons reveal no missing geometry, and a human reviewer can identify the goal in a blind five-second view.

   **Evidence:** **Acceptance contract (not observed):** after full-suite implementation lock, run a 30-minute session on D3 iPad A16/iPadOS 26.5, and record GPU frame timing, missed frames, thermals, visual captures and app crashes; reject or downscale if failed.

**Response:** Keep development gated: build the rule “Balance twin stars to keep orbiting flower worlds within a light zone” before polishing a trailer; measure solving, retries and user comprehension; compare the candidate against other shortlisted mechanisms.

**Kill / pivot criteria:** Stop or combine this idea if a seeded level has no meaningful choice, if real D3 renders fail sustained budgets after quality scaling, if distinctive visual assets require manual art, or if independent players cannot explain the rules. **Argument verdict:** **PROTOTYPE, NOT GUARANTEED LAUNCH.** The central claim is that a beautiful and interactive code-generated game is *testable*; its commercial desirability is still unproven.

## Evidence and interpretation limitations

Public market evidence applies to comparable existing titles or an entire paid-game category, not these unbuilt concepts. Hardware evidence describes supported instrumentation and ANGLE capabilities, not achieved quality. Every acceptance contract is a proposed experiment and should not be reported as a completed test. The competitive landscape must be rechecked for every title near its release date.

### 11.2. Original 500-game commercial research study (archived reference)
For context, the 500-game study below is carried inside this **one Markdown file** so Claude does not require a separate attachment. It is a prior selection artifact: engineering forecasts and commercial scores remain hypotheses, and its earlier implementation sketches are superseded by the executable game-specific designs in §6.
<!-- BEGIN RESEARCH STUDY REFERENCE: copied in full from Round-2-Refined-Premium-Games-Study-500.md -->
# VisualCore Premium 3D Games — Refined Round 2: 500 Candidates, Code-Only Graphics

**Research baseline:** November 10, 2026 · **Scope:** iOS/iPadOS · **VisualCore path:** existing OpenGL ES → ANGLE → Metal · **Business:** one upfront purchase, no advertising, ad SDKs, IAP or subscriptions.

**Scope of evidence:** 500 ideas assessed, **not** 500 researched apps and **not** 500 prototypes. Exactly 200 concepts preserve the previous research matrix; 300 genuinely new concepts were written and scored against declared genre/technical priors. Numeric scores are screening judgments and are not forecasts, experimental results, consumer surveys or audited sales.

## Executive decision: launch a portfolio of experiments, not 25 clones

The screening examined **500** concepts across **62** explicit scoring criteria. **249** pass every proposed code-only/visual/gameplay gate (**20** from the original 200; **229** from the new 300). **25** enter a diverse portfolio shortlist (**4** inherited; **21** newly proposed). Scores favor genuine shader and procedural spectacle, but *a top-25 ranking is a decision to prototype, not a commitment to publish every candidate*.

### Hard requirements

- Graphics originate in procedural geometry, signed distance fields, GLSL ES, parametric meshes, instancing, particles, lighting, algorithms and simulation. There are **zero AI-generated images**, photographic background plates, manually sculpted characters, purchased level art or commissioned texture requirements.
- Use **only the existing VisualCore / projectM-iOS rendering bridge**, through the established ANGLE Metal backend. Do not replace ANGLE, recreate an independent Metal renderer, or ship different backends for each game.
- The visual effect must materially embody a decision in gameplay: steering, folding, redirecting, growing, balancing, tuning or routing. A screensaver with a score counter does not qualify.
- Every game is complete for an upfront $1.99–$4.99 purchase; no ads anywhere, ad SDKs, rewarded screens, analytics ad identifiers, microtransactions, subscriptions, user accounts or live-services infrastructure.
- All physics and visual render loops are bounded and deterministic enough for automation and adaptive quality on D3. This is an *engineering estimate* pending instrumented device tests.
- A portfolio release must satisfy Apple’s originality and spam guidance: no clones of existing games, and no two VisualCore offerings that differ only by visuals or theme. Similar ideas should be merged into a single substantial game.

### Top 25 ordered for creative/technical prototyping

| # | Candidate | Mechanic family | Heuristic score | Visual score | Price | Distinguishing rule |

## 1. Market evidence: what is known, and what is not

- **The mobile gaming market is huge, but not a premium-sales forecast.** Sensor Tower’s [State of Gaming 2026](https://sensortower.com/press/press-release-sensor-tower-state-of-gaming-gaming-drove-52-billion-downloads-82b-iap-revenue-on-mobile-and-12b-premium-revenue-on-steam) reports approximately **$82 billion of 2025 mobile game in-app-purchase revenue** and approximately 52 billion game downloads across mobile, PC and consoles. That $82 billion figure does not represent purchases of upfront-priced iOS games. Gaming downloads per minute are a global scale statistic, not a customer acquisition forecast.

- **People demonstrably pay upfront for some mobile games.** Apple’s [2025 U.S. iPhone top-paid list](https://apps.apple.com/us/iphone/room/6756363168) includes Minecraft, Balatro, Geometry Dash, Bloons TD 6, Stardew Valley, and other recognizable products. Those titles are unusually established competitors; no percentage can be inferred for unknown VisualCore games.

- **Premium, calm, visually distinctive desktop mechanics have audience evidence.** [Tiny Glade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2198150/Tiny_Glade/) and [Dorfromantik](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1455840/Dorfromantik/) have real positive Steam customer reviews; [Mini Metro](https://store.steampowered.com/app/287980/Mini_Metro/) demonstrates a minimalist routing loop; [Glass Masquerade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/) shows demand for stylized art puzzles; [Poly Bridge 3](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1850160/Poly_Bridge_3/) shows engagement with construction-physics systems. These are **genre precedents, not proposals to copy**.

- **PC platform context, not sales attribution.** The [October 2026 Steam hardware survey](https://store.steampowered.com/hwsurvey/) reported approximately **93.70% Windows, 3.95% Linux and 2.35% macOS** among respondents. A game working across Windows/macOS/Linux helps demonstrate broad design appeal, but these percentages are neither revenue shares nor iOS conversion metrics.

- **Steam visibility does not equal predictable money.** SteamDB’s [relaxing-game catalog](https://steamdb.info/tag/1654/?min_reviews=500) exposes relative review/follower/peak-player measures; pricing and review counts are public but unit sales cannot be inferred reliably by simply multiplying reviews by a constant. This portfolio therefore does not invent per-candidate sales numbers.

### A platform-portability precedent (verified from product listings)

| Comparable PC product | Verified lesson | Porting caveat |
|---|---|---|
| [[Tiny Glade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2198150/Tiny_Glade/)] | Procedural diorama creation has strong positive reception; its official Steam store lists Windows, macOS and Linux requirements | Its rendering budgets, assets, controls and developer recognition do not automatically carry to iPhone |
| [[Mini Metro](https://store.steampowered.com/app/287980/Mini_Metro/)] | A small visual ruleset can deliver meaningful strategy without elaborate character animation | Its map-driven 2D interaction differs from three-dimensional spectacle |
| [[Dorfromantik](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1455840/Dorfromantik/)] | Geometry and systems can deliver relaxation with decision-making | Procedural 3D landscapes need device-level simplification |
| [[Glass Masquerade](https://store.steampowered.com/app/511470/Glass_Masquerade/)] | Art-led premium puzzles can accumulate a dedicated audience | A new 3D optics game must not mimic protected stained-glass motifs or arrangements |
| [[Poly Bridge 3](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1850160/Poly_Bridge_3/)] | Physics construction can support complete, rule-driven play | A phone needs shorter stages, cheaper simulation and touch-first controls |

## 2. Copyright, App Store policy and the danger of indistinguishable games

The [U.S. Copyright Office](https://www.copyright.gov/register/tx-games.html) says that a game idea or playing method is not itself protected by copyright, but specific artwork, text and other expression can be. This is not a license to reuse game code, exact levels, names, trademarks, audio, distinctive visual identity or copied marketing. Open-source licenses must be audited if any source is considered, and no code from other games is required for the shortlisted titles.

Apple [App Review Guidelines 4.1 and 4.3](https://developer.apple.com/app-store/review/guidelines/) flag copycats and repeated near-identical apps. **The goal is not to flood the App Store with 25 shader reskins.** For every candidate the product team must document one mechanic, one content structure and one user experience that differs materially from every other shipped app; merge overlapping ideas when they do not pass the distinctiveness review.

## 3. All 62 criteria, rubric and score calculation

Each criterion is rated on a **1–5 ordinal judgment scale** (1 = weak, 3 = plausible, 5 = strong). Decimal ratings indicate heuristic prioritization, *not measured accuracy*. Original 200 candidates retain their earlier 50 and 12 ratings; 300 new concepts receive scores from their old-category reference averages plus documented text/trait modifiers (see the included code). No row has its own directly observed purchase conversion data.

**Commercial/engineering subtotal:** `C = 20 × Σ(criterion_rating × original_weight × group_multiplier) / Σ(original_weight × group_multiplier)`, with multipliers Market 0.78, Competition 0.86, Premium 1.00, Experience 1.22, Engineering 1.29.

**Visual subtotal:** `V = 20 × Σ(visual_rating × visual_weight) / Σ(visual_weight)`. **Final screening score:** `0.30 × C + 0.70 × V`. The 70% weighting prioritizes code-generatable spectacle. **Eligibility is assessed independently before shortlisting**; an unqualified game cannot win by a high weighted average.
